summary: In late October 2021 Roblox was down for 73 hours after a Consul cluster, under heavy load and with a new streaming feature enabled, hit a database performance problem. Monitoring that depended on the same cluster made it harder to see.

overview.background: Roblox ran many services that rely on HashiCorp Consul for service discovery, health checks and key-value storage. On 27 October a streaming feature was enabled on the Consul backend that handles traffic routing.
systems: Consul cluster (five voters and five non-voters, upgraded from 1.9 to 1.10)
Telemetry and monitoring that used Consul
overview.impact: Players were gradually admitted back, reaching 100 percent at 16:45 PST on Sunday 31 October, 73 hours after the start.
overview.severity: Total platform outage for three days. Roblox does not publish a formal level.
overview.gaps: The post does not give player counts, the exact first-failure minute on 28 October, or raw logs.

archNote: The Consul cluster, the telemetry dependency and the single shared cluster are described in Roblox's post. Layout is ours.

diagrams.title: One Consul cluster under many workloads
diagrams.caption: Many services shared one Consul cluster. Telemetry also depended on it, so the tools for diagnosing it were affected.

diagrams.title: Roblox's stated direction (conceptual)
diagrams.caption: Roblox said it removed the circular dependency, added Consul and BoltDB alerts, moved to a new multi-zone data center and planned dedicated clusters. This is our picture of that direction.

nodes.label: Dedicated Consul cluster for other workloads
Alerts on Consul and BoltDB health

afterChanges: A problem in one workload no longer takes down others.
Monitoring survives the failure it must report.
Zone loss does not stop the control plane.
afterNote: Separate failure domains and independent monitoring are the two big shifts.
timelineNote: Times are PST as given in Roblox's post. Only times stated in the post are shown.

timeline.e: Streaming is enabled on the traffic-routing backend and its node count grows by 50 percent.
A Vault performance degradation and a Consul server with high CPU are noticed.
Players are at 50 percent of normal.
Most of the cluster runs on new 128-core machines but is still unhealthy.
The cluster is reset from a snapshot and health-check frequency is lowered from 60 seconds to 10 minutes.
Streaming is disabled everywhere. Median key-value write latency drops to 300 ms.
100 percent of players are readmitted, 73 hours after the start.

rootCause.trigger: Streaming was enabled on Consul while the system carried unusually high read and write load.
rootCause.underlying: Roblox's load triggered a pathological performance issue in BoltDB, the storage used by Consul.
contributing: One Consul cluster supported many workloads
Telemetry depended on Consul, a circular dependency
A recently upgraded Consul (1.9 to 1.10) was at an unusual load
Frequent health checks added work during the failure
propagation: Monitoring that needs Consul goes blind.

evidence.label: The streaming feature
evidence.body: Enabling a relatively new streaming feature on Consul under unusually high read and write load

evidence.label: The storage problem
evidence.body: our particular load conditions triggered a pathological performance issue in BoltDB

evidence.label: Shared fate
evidence.body: A single Consul cluster supporting multiple workloads exacerbated the impact of these issues.

evidence.label: Simulated Consul checks
evidence.body:
$ consul operator raft list-peers
Node      State     Voter
consul-1  leader    true
consul-2  follower  true
$ consul info | grep -E 'last_log|commit_index|applied_index'
evidence.note: Commands one would use to inspect Raft health. Output is invented.

diagnose.step: Check cluster leadership and write latency.
diagnose.why: Slow or flapping leaders mean the control plane is unhealthy.

diagnose.step: Look at storage-level latency on the servers.
diagnose.why: Roblox traced the issue to BoltDB behaviour.
A feature enabled the day before was a main clue.

correct.step: Disable the new feature across the system.
correct.why: Roblox disabled streaming everywhere before recovery.

correct.step: Reset the cluster from a known good snapshot if needed.
Reduce non-essential load, such as health-check frequency.
correct.why: Lowering frequency from 60 seconds to 10 minutes eased pressure.
Roblox used about 10 percent increments with DNS steering to avoid a stampede.

verify.step: Watch write latency and leader stability.
verify.why: Latency of 300 ms median was the sign streaming was no longer the problem.

verify.step: Confirm caches are warm before opening to everyone.
verify.why: Cold caches can cause a second overload.

prevent.step: Remove monitoring dependencies on the system being monitored.
prevent.why: You need to see in a crisis.

prevent.step: Alert on Consul and storage health.
Test new features under production-like load first.
prevent.why: Roblox planned to reintroduce streaming only after testing.

fix.safety: Resetting a cluster from a snapshot can lose recent writes. Take a copy of current state first, and let people in gradually. Do not restart everything at once.

troubleshoot.scenario: A key-value store that every service uses has slow writes and a high-CPU server. Dashboards that read from it are blank. A new feature was turned on yesterday.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do first, and how do you see what is happening?
hints: How do you add capacity safely?
troubleshoot.answer: Turn off the new feature, reduce background load such as health checks, use out-of-band tools to inspect the cluster, and avoid adding load by restarting everything. Plan a snapshot reset only if state is bad.

options: A new Consul streaming feature under heavy load triggered a BoltDB performance problem
rootcause.why: That is the cause Roblox states.

remediation.answer: Move telemetry onto infrastructure that does not need the system it monitors, or give it a separate path.
Use DNS steering to admit about 10 percent steps, watch metrics at each step, and hold if errors rise.

remediation.task: Write alerts for the control plane.
remediation.answer: Alert on leader changes, write latency, commit lag and storage health, with thresholds tested under load.

design.prompt: Design a service-discovery layer that survives one workload overloading it.
design.answer: Use separate clusters per critical workload, deploy across zones, keep monitoring off the cluster, apply quotas on request rates, and test new features under load before use.

checks.q: How long did the outage last?

checks.why: The post says the telemetry system relied on Consul.

options: To avoid a second overload as caches warm
checks.why: Roblox used DNS steering in about 10 percent increments.

monitoring: Alert on Consul and BoltDB health
recovery: Reset from snapshot as a last step
